learningObjective: Explain FP8 matmul semantics on Hopper Tensor Cores including accumulator dtype and scaling requirements.

canonicalClaims.claim: Hopper FP8 Tensor Core matmuls accumulate in FP32 for numerical stability; production FP8 pipelines rely on per-tensor or per-block scale factors managed by frameworks like NVIDIA Transformer Engine (DelayedScaling); FP8 peak throughput is ~2× BF16 in compute-bound kernels but only when memory bandwidth is not the bottleneck.
conditions: The target GPU has FP8 Tensor Cores (Hopper / Ada).
nonImplications: Does not imply FP8 matches BF16 accuracy without workload-specific care.
Does not imply the 2× peak is always realized — bandwidth-bound kernels see less.

misconceptions.claim: FP8 GEMM uses an FP8 accumulator to preserve full FP8 semantics.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Production Tensor Core FP8 GEMM accumulates in FP32 to avoid the tiny FP8 dynamic range overflowing on a long reduction.

misconceptions.claim: FP8 delivers 2× BF16 speedup automatically on any FP16 model.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP8 requires opt-in, scale-factor management, and often small algorithm changes; frameworks do not silently upgrade.

misconceptions.claim: FP8's small dynamic range acts as an implicit regularizer that improves accuracy.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP8's small range causes information loss unless scale factors keep values in range; there is no evidence of consistent regularization benefits.

misconceptions.claim: Because H100 FP8 peak is 2× BF16, every FP8 matmul is 2× faster in wall-clock than BF16.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Peak-throughput ratios apply only in compute-bound regimes; batch-1 decode and memory-bound kernels see much smaller gains.

implementationFacts: H100 WGMMA instruction supports E4M3/E5M2 inputs with FP32 accumulator.
Transformer Engine's DelayedScaling recipe uses per-tensor scale factors with lagged statistics.
H100 FP8 peak: ~1979 TFLOPS (sparse) / ~989 TFLOPS (dense); BF16 peak ~989/494.
performanceScenarios: LLaMA-70B training with Transformer Engine FP8 achieves ~1.5-1.8× wall-clock speedup vs BF16 on H100 clusters.
